Claude responded: The bug is a lifecycle ordering mistake: Register() is called in OnStartUp(), but that runs before a server connection exists.

The bug is a lifecycle ordering mistake: Register() is called in OnStartUp(), but that runs before a server connection exists. It works the first time only by accident — the initial connect happens shortly after startup, and some MOOS implementations re-send registrations on first connect. After a reconnect, however, OnConnectToServer() fires again but there's nothing there to re-register, so the subscription is silently lost.

The correct pattern
cpp
bool MyApp::OnStartUp()
{
    // Read config, initialize state — no Register() calls here
    return true;
}

bool MyApp::OnConnectToServer()
{
    Register("NAV_X", 0);   // Re-runs on every connect and reconnect
    return true;
}

Why this works: OnConnectToServer() is called by the MOOS machinery every time a (re)connection to the MOOSDB is established — including the very first one. Placing Register() here guarantees subscriptions are (re)declared to a live server each time, surviving any number of disconnects.

The general rule
Hook	Purpose
OnStartUp()	Read the mission file, allocate resources, set initial state
OnConnectToServer()	Declare all Register() calls — every time
Iterate()	Publish, compute, act

A useful mental model: treat OnConnectToServer() like a network socket's on_open callback. Just as you'd re-subscribe to topics when a WebSocket reconnects, you re-register here. Anything registered before the socket is open is gone the moment the connection drops.
